title: Pushing and pulling
summary: Pushing moves something away from us. Pulling brings it towards us. Both make our bodies strong.
body:
## Push or pull?

- **Push** — move something **away** from you: pushing a wheelbarrow, a door or a swing.
- **Pull** — move something **towards** you: pulling a rope, a bucket from a well or a drawer.

## Fun activities

1. **Tug of war**: two teams hold a rope and pull. The team that pulls the other over the line wins.
2. **Partner push**: stand facing a friend, palms together, and push gently. Who moves?
3. **Wall push**: push against a wall with straight arms. Count to 10.
4. **Pull the cart**: pull a box with a rope tied to it.

## Why push and pull?

These activities make your **arms, legs and back strong**, and stretching keeps your body **flexible**.

## Play safe

- Push and pull **gently**; never push a friend hard.
- Hold the rope firmly but let go if someone falls.
- Play on soft grass or sand.
activities:
1. Find three things you push and three things you pull at home.
2. Play tug of war with family members using a strong rope or cloth.
3. Do the wall push and count to 10, three times.
reflection: Was pushing or pulling harder for you today? Why do you think so?

quiz.question: Moving a door away from you is...
Getting a bucket of water out of a well is...
In tug of war, the teams...
Pushing and pulling make our bodies...

title: Reading sounds in words and sentences
summary: Letter-sound combinations like ai, ee and oa help us read and say new words correctly.
body:
## Vowel teams

When two vowels walk together, they often make **one long sound**.

| Letters | Sound | Words |
|---|---|---|
| **ai** | long /a/ | r**ai**n, tr**ai**n, p**ai**nt |
| **ee** | long /e/ | tr**ee**, s**ee**d, f**ee**t |
| **oa** | long /o/ | b**oa**t, g**oa**t, r**oa**d |

## Reading in sentences

Read these sentences aloud. Point to each word:

- *The* **goat** *is on the* **road**.
- *The* **rain** *makes the* **seed** *grow into a* **tree**.
- *We wait for the* **train**.

## Speaking clearly

- Look at the person you are talking to.
- Speak loudly enough for them to hear.
- Say each sound in the word.

Use the new words to tell a short story about a goat and a boat.
activities:
1. Write three words with "ee" and three with "oa".
2. Read the three sentences above to a family member.
3. Make up one sentence using the words "rain" and "tree".
reflection: Which new word was the hardest to say? Practise it three more times.

quiz.question: Which word has the 'ee' sound?
Which word has the 'oa' sound?
Fill in: The ___ makes the seed grow.
When you speak, you should...
options: Look at the listener and speak clearly

title: Clean beds, clean sleeping places
summary: We sleep on beddings made of local materials. Keeping them clean and aired keeps us healthy.
body:
## Our beddings

Beddings are things we sleep on or cover ourselves with:

- **Mattress** — foam, cotton or one made from grass or dry banana leaves
- **Mat** — woven from reeds, sisal or palm leaves
- **Blanket, sheet and pillow**
- **Mosquito net** — protects us from mosquitoes that spread malaria

## Keeping sleeping places clean

1. **Air** the mattress and blanket in the sun every week. Sunlight dries them and kills germs and bed bugs.
2. **Wash** sheets and pillowcases often.
3. **Sweep** under the bed. Do not keep food in the bedroom.
4. **Open the windows** during the day to let in fresh air.
5. **Tuck in** the mosquito net every night and mend any holes.

## Why it matters

Dirty beddings can have **bed bugs**, **fleas** and germs that cause itching and sickness. A clean bed helps us sleep well and wake up fresh.
activities:
1. Help take a blanket outside to air it in the sun.
2. Make your bed every morning this week.
3. Check your mosquito net for holes. Tell an adult if you find any.
reflection: What will you do every morning to keep your sleeping place clean?

quiz.question: Why do we air beddings in the sun?
options: Sunlight dries them and kills germs

quiz.question: A mosquito net protects us from...
Which is a local material for making mats?
What should we NOT keep in the bedroom?

title: Maamkuzi na maagano katika jamii
summary: Jamii hutumia maamkuzi mbalimbali kulingana na mtu, wakati na mahali. Tunayatumia ipasavyo.
body:
## Maamkuzi mbalimbali

| Hali | Maamkuzi | Jibu |
|---|---|---|
| Kwa mtu mzima | **Shikamoo** | **Marahaba** |
| Kwa rafiki | **Mambo?** / **Vipi?** | **Poa.** / **Safi.** |
| Kwa watu wengi | **Hamjambo?** | **Hatujambo.** |
| Mgonjwa | **Pole! Unaendeleaje?** | **Ninaendelea vizuri, asante.** |
| Mtu aliyefanya kazi | **Pole na kazi!** | **Asante.** |

**Kumbuka:** "Mambo" na "Vipi" ni kwa marafiki tu. Kwa mwalimu au mzazi, tunasema "Shikamoo" au "Hujambo".

## Maagano

- **Kwaheri ya kuonana!**
- **Safari njema!** (kwa mtu anayesafiri)
- **Lala salama!**
- **Tutaonana Jumatatu!**

## Adabu

Tunapoamkua, tunamtazama mtu, tunatabasamu na tunasubiri ajibu.
activities:
1. Andika maamkuzi matatu ya kumwamkua mtu mzima na matatu ya rafiki.
2. Mwambie mtu aliyepika chakula leo "Pole na kazi!"
3. Igiza: rafiki yako anasafiri. Mwage kwa "Safari njema!"
reflection: Kwa nini hatumwamkui mwalimu kwa kusema 'Mambo'?

quiz.question: Mtu akisema 'Hamjambo?' mnajibu...
Tunamwambia nini mtu anayesafiri?
Maamkuzi 'Mambo?' yanafaa kwa...
Tunamwambia nini mtu aliyekuwa akifanya kazi?

title: First, second, third: position of things
summary: We use ordinal numbers like 1st, 2nd and 3rd to show the position of things in a line.
body:
## Ordering by size

We can put things in order from the **smallest to the biggest**, or from the **biggest to the smallest**.

## Position in a line

When children stand in a line, each one has a **position**:

| Position | In symbols | In words |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **1st** | first |
| 2 | **2nd** | second |
| 3 | **3rd** | third |
| 4 | **4th** | fourth |
| 5 | **5th** | fifth |
| 10 | **10th** | tenth |
| 20 | **20th** | twentieth |

Notice: 1**st**, 2**nd**, 3**rd**, and then most end in **th** (4th, 5th, 6th ... 20th). But 21st, 22nd and 23rd follow the first three again.

## Example

In a race, Achieng finished **1st**, Musa finished **2nd** and Wanjiru finished **3rd**. Achieng won!

Our days at school also have positions: **Monday** is the 1st school day, **Friday** is the 5th.
activities:
1. Line up 5 objects. Say the position of each one: first, second, third...
2. Write the positions 1st to 10th in symbols and in words.
3. Ask your family members to stand in a line by height. Who is 1st? Who is last?
reflection: Where do we use positions in real life? (Think of races, queues and class.)

quiz.question: How do we write 'third' in symbols?
Musa finished after Achieng, who was 1st. Musa was...
'Fifth' in symbols is...
Which day is the 5th school day of the week?
